opening.headline: When you receive a notice of model discontinuation, learn how to read the notice and how to respond accordingly to our service.
body: Assume we have received a notice from the provider stating that a model currently in use has been discontinued. The notice includes the model name and date, but it does not specify which of our services is calling that model. Without knowing the affected scope, we cannot begin reviewing alternative models or coordinating timelines.

In this lesson, we first examine the common structure found in the end-of-support documentation from Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic. Then, we learn how to read the notice period and model ID meanings, how to interpret each item in the notice as a service impact, and verify the differences in response when a model list is available versus when it is not.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: We can describe the structure of the support termination policies of the three companies.
The Jongjong notification item can be analyzed in relation to service impacts and responses.

screens.title: An announcement from Danjong has come, but I don't know the affected scope.
screens.lead: First, read the status of the team that received the notice from Danjong. While reading, think about what is lacking.

visual.alt: Notice of model discontinuation: a scene showing one frame and three services marked with question marks beneath it.

paragraphs: One day, an email from the provider arrived. It stated that the model currently in use had been discontinued, with a termination date and a recommended replacement model provided. The three companies explained that they would notify affected customers via email and documentation based on the model. However, our organization operates based on service criteria, not model-based notifications.

We must be able to immediately identify which of our services uses that model. However, in reality, services that hardcode the model name in their code, services that store the model name in configuration files, and services called by other teams are all intermixed. Without knowing the scope of impact, we cannot begin alternative model reviews or scheduled discussions.
This course covers two topics: first, how to read termination notices, and second, how to map those notices to our service.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: What could be prepared before the announcement arrives? We return to this question at the end of class.

screens.outro: First, let me recall the current readiness status of my organization.

screens.title: Do you have a list of currently used models?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You won't have to enter or submit your answer, so think about it in your head first and then press it.

items.prompt: Do you have a list of currently deployed models? Is that list including service name, model ID, call path, and responsible team?
items.answer: To respond to an announcement, the list must include at least the service name, model ID, call path, and responsible team. The model ID serves as the key to match the announcement, and the responsible team is the party responsible for scheduling. If any of these four fields is missing, it becomes difficult to promptly determine the impacted scope on the day the announcement is received.

items.prompt: What happens if we only specify an alias instead of the model ID?
items.answer: A alias is a convenient name referring to a specific snapshot. Simply listing an alias makes it difficult to associate the alias with the actual snapshot it refers to or with the expiration date of that snapshot. Therefore, it is safer to list both the alias and the actual ID in the list.

items.prompt: Who verifies that this list is up to date?
items.answer: The list is not a one-time document. It changes every time the service updates or redefines its model. If there is no designated person responsible for verification or a defined review cycle, the list quickly becomes out of sync with reality. This course concludes that without a model list, there is no corresponding response.

data.notes: All three companies provide common model information, end dates, and recommended replacement models. Anthropic explains that partner platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud set their own end dates, meaning that even the same model may have different statuses and dates.

screens.outro: Now that I understand the structure, I'll read about how the notification period and model ID alter the meaning of the notice.

screens.title: The notification period and model ID have been affected.
screens.lead: The following is a hypothetical model usage overview by service. By selecting the displayed section, you can view how each model ID or name affects the termination notice reading process.

visual.alt: A diagram contrasting a structure where a nickname refers to a dated snapshot versus a structure where a dateless ID refers to the snapshot itself.
labels: All IDs have their own expiration schedules.

data.text:
Service A: model = claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929  
Service B: model = claude-sonnet-4-5  # alias  
Service C: model = claude-sonnet-4-6  
Service D: model = computer-use-preview  
Service E: model = gpt-5.3-codex

marks.note: 4.6 This is an ID associated with the date of the previous model. This ID itself represents a snapshot and has a unique expiration schedule. If the same string appears in the notice, it means service A is directly affected.

A nickname without a date. In models prior to 4.6, it was a convenient name referring to the most recent date snapshot of the same minor version. When reading announcements, you must verify which snapshot this nickname currently refers to and align it with the corresponding schedule of that snapshot.

4.6 IDs for generations thereafter are in a format without dates. However, instead of being pointers that continuously change with the latest models, they are fixed snapshots. Updated versions appear with new IDs, each of which also has its own expiration date.

This is an OpenAI model named with "preview" in its name. The documentation states that the preview model may be terminated abruptly with a notice period as short as two weeks, and advises against using it for core business operations if immediate migration is not possible. The shorter the notice period, the higher the service priority.

This is an example of a specialized variant classified under general provision models. OpenAI explains that a notice period of at least six months is required for general provision models and at least three months for specialized variants. The notice period may be shorter if safety or compliance reasons apply.

screens.outro: Now that we can understand the meaning of IDs, we will proceed with the procedure of translating announcements into service impact.

screens.title: Table showing translation based on service impact
screens.lead: Select the right arrow to verify, in sequence, which item in the service list each notice item affects.

steps.title: The model ID in the notice is a search key.
steps.body: Use the model ID specified in the notice as a key to find entries in the model inventory that have the same ID. Since multiple services might use the same ID, you must locate all rows rather than just one.

steps.title: The deadline is the service-specific due date.
steps.body: Move the notice expiration date to a service-specific deadline. The shorter the notice period, the higher the service's priority. For example, Anthropic commits to providing at least 60 days' notice before the public launch of its models, while OpenAI's preview models may have as short as two weeks.

steps.title: The recommended alternative model is only a candidate.
steps.body: The alternative model proposed by the provider is a previous candidate. There is no guarantee that it has the same purpose or quality. Anthropic also recommends thoroughly testing the new model before its documentation ends.

steps.title: Collects impacted service list
steps.body: The Impact Services List includes a table containing the responsible party, call path, and user impact scope. Having this list enables alternative model evaluation and scheduling coordination to be conducted on a service-by-service basis.

steps.title: Cross-verifies actual usage locations.
steps.body: Anthropic guides how to download API keys and model usage details in CSV format by selecting Export on the Usage page of the Claude Console. By matching this usage data with inventory records, you can identify usage instances not documented in the records.

screens.outro: Now that I know the translation method, I'll follow a real notice from beginning to end.

screens.title: Explanation: The process of identifying affected services after notice receipt
screens.lead: The instructor walks through the process of identifying impacted services by following one notification. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: case
steps.body: We have received a notice stating that a certain model has been deprecated with a specified shutdown date. For example, in Anthropic's documentation, it states that claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 will be discontinued on November 30, 2026, with the recommended alternative model claude-sonnet-5-5.

steps.title: Create a search term
steps.body: Move the notice's model ID, date, and recommended replacement model into the inventory search fields. Search for the model ID using the exact string, place the date in the expiration field, and pre-place the replacement model in the candidate field.

steps.title: Cross-verify by code and usage.
steps.body: Search for the corresponding ID string in code, configuration files, and deployment variables. Then cross-reference with the usage logs to identify the actual service being called. Searching only for the string may fail to detect paths called by external teams.

steps.title: Let's expand the alias.
steps.body: A service that uses aliases verifies what snapshot the alias points to. Aliases in models prior to 4.6 point to the most recent date snapshot, so the service compares whether that snapshot's ID matches the specified ID.

steps.title: Fill in the affected services list
steps.body: Each service's owner, expiration date, and replacement candidate are filled into the affected service list. In this case, services with shorter notice periods are placed higher up.

steps.title: result
steps.body: Once the list is completed, you can immediately proceed to the next steps: alternative model evaluation and scheduling coordination. Once this stage is completed on the day the notice is received, the schedule will be in a coordinatable state.

screens.outro: Now, let's look at how the same notification is processed differently when there is no model list.

screens.title: Explanation: Delay in response when no model list is available
screens.lead: Compare how the response differs when transitioning between two states for the same notification.

states.label: If a list exists
states.body:
Notice: When searching for the relevant model ID in the daily inventory, the impacted service is immediately confirmed. Since each service already has an assigned owner, the deadline can be scheduled immediately, and the alternative model evaluation can begin right away.

By linking the inventory with periodic checks that read OpenAI's `GET /v1/models` and `shutdown_date` fields, you can identify models whose end dates have been announced—even if you miss the notice email. If the fields are null, the model has not yet announced its end date.

The minimum fields required in the inventory are model ID, call path, and responsible team.

states.label: In the absence of a list
states.body:
The notice provides only the model name, so we have to search for it ourselves. Most of our time is spent searching the entire code repository, contacting team members, and checking usage logs. Alternative model evaluation can only begin after identification is complete.

When notice periods are short, the risk increases. Preview models may be terminated with as little as a two-week notice, meaning delayed identification can quickly lead to service outages.

Therefore, the statement "there is no response if there is no model list" holds true.

The biggest difference between the two states lies in what is done during the first day after receiving the notice. If a list exists, that day is used for alternative model evaluation and scheduling coordination; if no list exists, the same day is spent trying to determine who is using that model. The termination date approaches equally in both cases, so the time available for evaluation and transition decreases by the amount of time spent on identification.

screens.outro: Since we've confirmed the difference between the two states, I'll now summarize the previous content into a single coherent flow.

screens.title: Read End-of-Support Policy: Structure and Response
screens.lead: Summarizes how to read each company's policy and outlines the corresponding response flow—all in one place. Review it by substituting it into your own organization.

paragraphs: Read the common structure. Termination documents are read as model, termination schedule, recommended alternative model, and notice period. Although the terminology differs among the three companies, all four elements are present in each.

Distinguishes between warnings and shutdowns. deprecated indicates a warning that a feature is no longer recommended, but the model still operates. shutdown or retired indicates a termination, after which subsequent requests will fail. The period during which a feature remains available is from the date the warning is received until the shutdown date.

Distinguishes between aliases and fixed IDs. Assuming that an ID without a date represents the latest update is incorrect. IDs from the 4.6 generation and later represent a fixed snapshot, while aliases from earlier generations refer to the most recent snapshot. Each ID has its own expiration schedule.

**Announcements need a list of affected services to be meaningful.** The model inventory includes services, model IDs, call paths, and responsible parties. With such a list, announcements can transition into targeted response plans with specific service schedules and assigned responsibilities.

callout.label: organizing
callout.text: The most effective preparation you can make before the notice arrives is to create and keep your model inventory up to date.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded or graded.
checks.q: There is a service that calls a model ID without a date, similar to Anthropic 4.6 models. What is the correct interpretation of the termination notice?
options: An ID without a date always points to the latest model, so it is not affected by end-of-life notifications.
An ID without a date is still a fixed snapshot, so its own expiration schedule must be verified.
An ID without a date does not need to be listed in the inventory since it has no expiration date.
ID without a date automatically transitions to a recommended replacement model at termination, no action is required.
checks.explain: An ID without a date is not an evergreen pointer but a fixed snapshot, and all IDs have their own expiration schedules. Therefore, impact must be read per ID.

wrong.0: A pointer that follows the latest update without a date is not a dynamic pointer; it is a fixed snapshot.
wrong.2: All IDs must have their own expiration dates and must be explicitly listed in the inventory.
wrong.3: Upon termination, automatic replacement does not occur; instead, the recommended replacement model is only a candidate, and quality verification and the actual transition must be performed manually.

checks.correctFeedback: Yes. An ID without a date is a fixed snapshot.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Think about it again. Having no date and staying up to date are different things.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded or graded.

right: Reserved as a backup candidate, quality is verified separately.
Table containing the responsible party, call path, and user impact scope

Services with earlier due dates and shorter notification periods have higher priority.
checks.explain: Each item in the notice must be matched with inventory to establish a service-specific schedule and assigned responsibilities for the corresponding action plan.
checks.correctFeedback: Yes. I have accurately connected all pairs.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Some pairs do not match. Think about which slot in the inventory each item belongs to.

checks.q: After receiving the notice, review the process of identifying affected services in the correct order.
items: The notice's model ID, date, and recommended alternative model are transferred as search terms.
Find the ID in Code, Settings, and Deployment Variables, and cross-verify with usage history.
A service that uses aliases verifies the snapshot that the alias points to.
Each service fills the affected service list with its responsible party, expiration date, and backup candidate.
checks.explain: Create a search term, find and verify actual usage contexts, resolve aliases, and finally compile a list.
checks.correctFeedback: Yes. This is the sequence from identification to consolidation.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Let's take a closer look at the sequence. First, identify the target object, then verify the usage context.

glossary.def: This is an announcement stating it is no longer recommended. The model is still operational but subject to an end date.
The model or endpoint is in a completely shutdown state where it can no longer be called. Anthropic refers to this as Retired.
The previous target candidates provided by the vendor together with the notice. Quality must be verified separately.
This is the minimum period that the provider notifies in advance before termination, and it may vary depending on the model type.
This is a list showing which model ID is called via which path for each service.

misconceptions.myth: You'll never be late even if you check when the notice comes.
misconceptions.fact: Without a list, the service identification process consumes the timeline. Especially in models with short notification periods, identification delays become outages.

misconceptions.myth: A model ID without a date is always updated to the latest model.
misconceptions.fact: 4.6 Snapshot IDs from generations after 4.6 are fixed snapshots. IDs without dates from models prior to 4.6 refer to the most recent date-based snapshot; these two must be distinguished when reading.

misconceptions.myth: Preview models can also be used for a long time like official models.
misconceptions.fact: OpenAI stated that preview models may be terminated with as short as two-week notice, and advises against using them for core business operations if they are not transferable.

closing.lead: This summarizes the core content of the class.
points: If there is no model list, there is no corresponding entry.
End document is read by model, schedule, alternate model, notice period.
The notice must be translated into an affected services list to become effective.
